statements.t: At September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, the Company did not record any credit impairment charges on its securities portfolio and attributed the unrealized losses primarily due to fluctuations in general interest rates or changes in expected prepayments and not due to credit quality.
Management will continue to proactively take steps to mitigate risk in the loan portfolio.

The guidance does not establish specific CRE lending limits; rather, it promotes sound risk management practices and appropriate levels of capital that will enable institutions to continue to pursue CRE lending in a safe and sound manner.
The Company’s regulatory capital ratios continue to be strong and in excess of regulatory minimum requirements to be considered well-capitalized as defined by regulators and internal Company targets.

The provision for credit losses is reviewed by management based upon our evaluation of economic and business conditions affecting our key lending areas and other conditions, such as new loan products, credit quality trends (including trends in nonperforming loans expected to result from existing conditions), collateral values, loan volumes and concentrations, specific industry conditions using reasonable and…

The decrease of $2.3 million in the provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 was determined by a number of factors, including paydowns in the loan portfolio, changes in the loan portfolio mix, a decrease in unfunded commitments, and Management’s consideration of existing economic conditions, including a slight improvement in…

The provision for credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was determined by a number of factors, including paydowns in the loan portfolio, changes in the loan portfolio mix, a decrease in unfunded commitments, and Management’s consideration of existing economic conditions, including a slight improvement in the quarterly economic outlook from the Federal Reserve Bank.

The Company does not anticipate engaging in any activities, either currently or over the long-term, for which adequate funding would not be available and which would therefore result in significant pressure on liquidity.
Based on the Company’s deposit retention experience and current pricing strategy, we anticipate that a significant portion of these time deposits will remain on deposit.
We monitor our liquidity position frequently and anticipate that it will have sufficient funds to meet our current funding commitments for the next 12 months and beyond.
Principal payments expected to be made on our lease liabilities during the twelve months ended September 30, 2027 totaled $1.5 million.
